[[Flatwoods monster]] }} '''Aliens''' are extraterrestrial creatures from unknown planets. This article serves as an overview of all alien appearances across the ''Fallout'' series. For the most prominent alien species, see [[Zetan]]s. ==Background==
The origins of aliens in the ''Fallout'' world are unclear. Two motherships, ''[[Zeta]]'' and an [[Support mothership|unnamed craft]], are known to be in orbit as of [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2277|2277]]. The Zetans have been engaging with [[human]]kind as early as the 1600s, but attracted little attention for most of human history. Belief in alien contact on Earth was initially limited to "crackpot" [[Conspiracy theory|conspiracy theorists]]. However, after the abduction of the USSA space capsule ''[[Clarabella 7]]'' and the pilot astronaut [[Hartigan|Colonel Hartigan]] during the 1960s [[Wikipedia:Space Race|Space Race]], the notion of alien existence became part of [[United States of America|American]] pop culture. Groups like [[Quaere Verum]] emerged in pre-War America as alien conspiracies gained national recognition. Rumors have spread that alien [[technology]] was the basis of many of the [[Enclave]]'s more exotic and impressive weaponry and robotics.[[Fallout 3 Official Game Guide]] Game of the Year Edition p.45: '''''Aliens'''''
''"Once thought to be covered up by a government conspiracy and believed only by 'crackpot' groups such as the Quaere Verum, evidence of extraterrestrial life can be traced back throughout human history, but became nationally recognized after the mysterious disappearance of the Clarabella 7 space pod during the 1960s Space Race. It is said that Alien technology was the basis of many of the Enclave's more exotic and impressive weaponry and robotics, and even toy manufacturers such as Wilson Automatoys weren't immune to these accusations. Recently, after the discovery of an Alien body in Fort Bannister, the shocking truth was revealed. The Aliens are not only real and alive, but they're back. And they're pissed."''
([[Fallout 3 Official Game Guide faction profiles]]) Even toy manufacturers such as [[Wilson Atomatoys]] were not immune to accusations of alien contact, but these conspiracies were most prominently associated with the [[United States government]], often accused of covering up knowledge of alien life. Alien specimens and technology were alleged to be kept largely in [[Area 51]]. At least one [[flying saucer]] was confirmed to be kept there, but it was re-captured by aliens at some point before being crashed in [[New California]], instantly killing the two alien pilots.[[Alien Ship]] The [[Brotherhood of Steel]][[Scribe (Fallout)|Scribe]]: ''"{111}{}{I've seen an alien space ship before.}"''
([[GENSCRIB.MSG|Scribe's dialogue]]) around [[Timeline#2161|2161]] and the [[Shi]]The [[Chosen One]]: ''"{176}{}{Xeno program.}"''
[[Shi Emperor]]: ''"{182}{}{'The subject on which we had hoped to establish a series of meaningful experiments has disappeared, presumed either destroyed or stolen by the Hubologists. Further inquiries have proven fruitless. Until such time as further specimens are obtained, this database will remain inoperative.' - Dr. Sheng}"''
([[Fsempter.msg|Shi Emperor's dialogue]]) around [[Timeline#2241|2241]] encountered the bodies of aliens or their spaceships. Additionally, in 2277, the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 3)|Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel]] have a moderate amount of [[alien power cell]]s kept in [[the Citadel]]'s hidden armory,Only accessible if the Citadel is targeted during [[Who Dares Wins]]. while the [[Brotherhood Outcasts]] also have some alien power cells at [[Fort Independence]]. Also, before 2277, an alien body was discovered in [[Fort Bannister]], likely by the Enclave, who transported what may have been recovered (including an [[alien blaster]] and some alien power cells) in the armory of the [[mobile base crawler]] at [[Adams Air Force Base]]. Some of the most advanced human technologies were created by using alien technology, like the [[Artificial intelligence|AI]] project number 59234, also known as [[Skynet]], which was created in the 2050s and manages the entire [[Sierra Army Depot]],The [[Chosen One]]: ''"Artificial intelligence?"''
[[Skynet]]: ''"Skynet was conceived and developed in the year 2050. Through the use of alien technology a new thinking computer was perfected. In the year 2081, Skynet became self-aware. In 2120 Skynet was given a new set of instructions and then abandoned by the Makers."''
([[WSTERM3B.MSG|Skynet main interface terminal's dialogue]]) and (allegedly) a device blocking telepathic and psychic commands, the [[Psychic nullifier (Fallout)|psychic nullifier]].[[Fallout Official Survival Guide]] p. 128: '''"Psychic Nullifier''': ''A strange device, possibly the product of alien technology. It blocks telepathic or psychic commands."''
([https://kupdf.net/download/fallout1-official-survival-guide_5908b975dc0d609854959e77_pdf Fallout guide on kupfd.net])
==Species== ===Bone aliens=== [[File:FlyingSaucer.png|right|200px]] {{Gamearticle|type=mentioned|FO1}}
These aliens appear only in the ''[[Fallout]]'' [[Fallout special encounters|special encounter]] "[[Alien Ship]]" and are distinguished by their small skeletons in proportion to their overly large skulls. The [[Vault Dweller]] can come upon this unique occurrence in the [[wasteland]] of [[New California]]. Level 4 of [[the Glow]] contains some of the most secretive research projects in the United States, including the study of captured [[Zetan]] aliens. A body of one such creature is still found near a suspension tube by ZAX's mainframe.[[Jesse Heinig]] on the [[Modiphius Entertainment|Modiphius]] Discord server: ''"I put the [[Zetan]] skeleton there to show that the Glow was the advanced R&D facility where they had the most secret and most unusual projects (we didn't call it a 'Zetan' at the time, just an alien)"''
{{clear}} ===Zeta aliens=== [[File:Alien.png|right|120px]] {{Gamearticle|link=Alien|FO3|FNV|FO4|FO76}}
[[Zetan]] aliens are the only extraterrestrials that could be considered a faction.
Aliens are relatively small, green-yellowish-skinned humanoid beings with no primary sex characteristics. Their bodies are elongated with a small chest, are lean, and lack any muscular definition. They also display no body hair of any kind. Their legs are shorter and jointed differently than a normal [[human]] and their limbs are also proportionally different than a normal humanoid; their humerus and femurs are the same lengths as their forearms and tibias. Their heads are unusually large in proportion to their bodies and have no noticeable outer ears or noses, instead only having small orifices for ears and nostrils. They have very wide mouths, no teeth, a light green tongue, and large opaque black eyes with no discernible iris or pupil. Their hands have only three long suctioned-cupped fingers and no thumbs, however, their fingers are so long they can wrap around objects and use any objects like any other humanoid species. They seem to breathe a similar atmosphere to that of Earth.A live [[Alien (Fallout 4)|alien]] in ''Fallout 4'' is seen in a cave with no helmet or breathing apparatus. Processing nutrients through the body with green blood, their diet includes unknown [[alien worm food|worm]] and [[alien squid food|squid food]].

{{clear}} ===Flatwoods monster=== {{Gamearticle|FO76|link1=Flatwoods monster}} [[File:Flatwoods monster NIF.png|right|200px]] The [[Cryptids|cryptid]] known as the [[Flatwoods]] monster is a Zetan encased in a purple space helmet, which obscures its face save for its glowing white eyes. The rest of the body is sealed in a protective suit, with an armored breathing apparatus and a large spade-shaped frill on its back. Flatwoods monsters have no visible legs, the suit instead terminating to a bullet-shaped point at its bottom, with what appear to be small hover-jets around the waist, allowing the creatures to float above the ground. A Flatwoods monster's long arms are tipped with large, three-fingered hands clad in large black gloves. {{clear}} {{FO2CC}} ===Decomposing alien=== [[File:Bodyitem.gif|right]] {{Gamearticle|FO2|link1=Decomposing body}}

{{pagelist|hidens=always|Alien technology|3}} ==Notes== The creatures that are known as [[wanamingo]]s are referred to as aliens but are actually the result of genetic engineering by humans and have nothing to do with aliens. ==Appearances== Aliens appear {{in|FO1}}, {{in|FO2|noin}}, {{in|FO3|noin}}, {{in|FNV|noin}}, {{in|FO4|noin}}, {{in|FO76|noin}}, {{in|FOS|noin}} and {{in|FWW|noin}}. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quotation|I put the Zetan skeleton there to show that the Glow was the advanced R&D facility where they had the most secret and most unusual projects (we didn't call it a "Zetan" at the time, just an alien) (...) The original Fo was not strongly designed to deal with aliens, obviously flying saucers and little green men with bulbous heads are part of the genre but there was enough going on without leaning into that, so it was just an additional "spice" to fit the motifs of the game. The later development of Zetans as a formalized part of the setting by Bethesda was just them expanding on that area of the 50s sci-fi. Of course they had to make a model for their engine and decide on a story and all of that. For our purposes in Fo1, it was just "Hey, let's put an alien skeleton in and scale it so it looks like one of those 50s sci-fi movie aliens."|[[Jesse Heinig]], [https://discord.com/channels/918602011631550526/918603704133881877/1127704898222440588 Messages] in the [https://discord.com/channels/918602011631550526/918603704133881877/1127708558373437480 Modiphius Discord]}}
Aliens in ''Fallout 3'' were designed to resemble stereotypical representations of aliens known as "[[Wikipedia:Grey alien|Roswell Greys]]," sometimes referred to as Zeta Reticulans.[https://web.archive.org/web/20090623052214/http://www.thehachiko.com/node/2300 The Hachiko Interview With Joel Burgess & Jeff Gardiner]: ''Players who found the UFO also found the remains of the pilot, who looks like the old school Roswell grays for the most part. Are these the same models being used for Mothership Zeta? Will the grays be the only enemies or are there a variety of new aliens to fight side-by-side with the gray pilot witnessed in the retail game?''
[[Jeff Gardiner]]: ''"Yes, we're modeling the same basic enemy after the 'Roswell grays.' There are other enemies that will be uncovered as well, including alien robotics."''

They wear distinguishable clothing such as [[Miner uniform|work clothes]], [[police uniform]]s, and professional wear rather than just indeterminate rags. Some feral ghouls have area-dependent apparel, such as feral ghouls wearing golf outfits at the [[Whitespring Resort]]. Unlike the [[Scorched]], which have retained greater cerebral functions and motor skills, feral ghouls are unable to use weapons due to the loss of mental and motor functions associated with their feral state. ==Characteristics== ===Biology=== [[File:FO76 Weak feral ghoul.png|thumb|right|100x200px]] Feral ghouls were formerly [[human]]s who suffered [[Radiation#Mutations|mutations]] due to radiation, including brain decay, resulting in complete loss of reason due to diminished mental functions. Their skin is slightly decomposed and their hair has almost disappeared. They live in groups wandering in nature or human infrastructures in search of future prey, whether human or animal, to feed on their flesh. It is rare to see ghouls wandering alone and the presence of a single ghoul is a sign of the presence of other ghouls in the vicinity. Sometimes a group of ghouls can be accompanied by a [[wendigo]]. The ghouls are friendly to the wendigos and show no sign of aggression towards them. Ghouls have a natural resilience to the [[Scorched Plague]]. ===Gameplay attributes=== Feral ghouls will attack most other creatures they encounter, with the exception of wendigos. They will attack charging and striking their opponents. Their attacks are always accompanied by [[Radiation|radiation damage]], with glowing ones inflicting increased radioactive damage. Withered, gangrenous and [[Fallout 76 diseases|diseased]] ({{icon|disease|20px}}) feral ghouls will also deal [[Poison|poison damage]]. All ghouls have a flat 15% chance to transmit [[Fallout 76 diseases|rad worms]] to the player character on-hit. * Unarmed: {{icon|attack}} 7 - 180 * Radiation: {{icon|radiation}} 3 - 110 * Poison: {{icon|acid}} 1 per second ({{icon|dur}} 5 sec) Ghouls often prepare their attacks by advancing slowly towards their opponent before running very quickly (often faster than the player character) and throwing themselves at their target in an exaggerated lunge. When adjacent, ghouls will perform a single and multi slap attacks. Jeff Gardiner and Ferret Baudoin are here today to answer your questions and chat about Wastelanders."] ''Reddit''. Retrieved April 23, 2020.
''"Yes, they are the same Floaters from before. FEV research was being done both in Appalachia and the West Coast.
In the earlier Fallouts they added a great tactical dimension to Super Mutant encounters. And they do the same for us. :)"'' Floaters are known to be friendly toward [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)|super mutants]] and behave almost as domesticated hunting companions, similar to [[Mutant hound (Fallout 76)|mutant hounds]]. Some floaters that encountered super mutants in the wilderness even began to follow the roving gangs.Super mutant 1: ''"Look at that smile. I think it like you! I know it ugly, but it friend."''
Super mutant 2: ''"It follow us here, but no attack, it need friend."''
Floater: ''"Gloooooorrrp! Bleghk?"''
Mutant 1: ''"What it say? I think it want to play."''
Mutant 2: ''"Or hungry. Maybe play with food like human?"''
([[Super mutant (Fallout 76)/Dialogue#W05 RE Camp JP16 SuperMutantsAndFloater|Super mutant dialogue]]) ==Characteristics== ===Biology=== Floaters are large, soft-bodied invertebrates, named after the flotation sacs that allow them to hover in the air. Noxious, flammable gases are generated by the creature and stored in the large flotation bladders atop their heads, giving the creature its distinctive appearance and ability to hover.[[Fallout 76 loading screens|''Fallout 76'' loading screens]]: ''"The enigmatic and deadly mutant creatures known as Floaters store noxious gases in their floatation bladders, which allow them to move through the air in search of prey."'' When killed, floaters bring their arms to their head and emit a loud shriek as the flotation sac violently expands. Upon rupturing, the explosion spreads volatile entrails in a large radius, leaving a lingering pool for a short duration. The explosion causes either poison damage (green), cryo damage and slower movement (blue), or fire damage (orange). These explosions, especially from flamers, can potentially kill other targets very easily if they stand too close, especially if their health is low. ===Gameplay attributes=== Floaters primarily hunt using ambush tactics, burrowing beneath the ground and lying in wait for prey. They leave their long tongues sticking out of the dirt and emit a bright, colorful mist to attract curious prey. When provoked, the floater leaps out from under the ground with its mouth gaping open in an attempt to intimidate and startle the prey. ====Elemental affinity==== Appalachian floaters have developed elemental abilities. Floaters have either acidic-based, incendiary-based, or cryogenic-based capabilities, primarily stored in the sacs covering the body and limbs. This pus can be harvested and turned into volatile grenades, which, when thrown, emulate the dying explosion of a critically wounded floater. Gnasher floaters are green in color and use acid-based attacks, releasing highly corrosive pus with every bite. Unlike other floater variants, gnashers cannot utilize ranged attacks and instead opt for melee combat. Flamer floaters are orange in color and are capable of long range fire-based attacks. Freezer floaters are bright blue in color and specialize in cryogenic attacks. Freezer pus is kept at low temperatures and can be sprayed at will in a large radius, causing damage to any technological parts it comes into contact with. ==Variants== ===Floater flamer=== [[Appalachia]] }} '''Flies''' are [[Creature|insects]] of the order ''Musca domestica'', known to live throughout North America, from [[New California]] to [[the Commonwealth]]. ==Characteristics== Unlike most [[Bloatfly|bloatflies]], the common house fly weathered [[Great War|the apocalypse]] without significant mutations. Their ecological niche remains unaltered as well, serving a vital role in the consumption of detritus. Much to the irritation of [[ghoul]]s, this means that flies feed on the nutrients of their rotting bodies.The [[Chosen One]]: ''"{115}{}{Why are the flies coming here?}"''
[[Eric (Broken Hills)|Eric]]: ''"{124}{}{They come here because for some odd reason I exude fly nutrients. My body is rich with food for them, and this sweating just makes it worse.}"''
The Chosen One: ''"{125}{}{That's just plain nasty. Why not take a bath or something?}"''
Eric: ''"{128}{}{I've tried that. I've tried everything. The only thing that keeps the flies off me is not to sweat... and when I don't have enough power to keep cool, I can't.}"''
([[Hceric.msg]])[[Eric (Broken Hills)|Eric]]'s character description: ''"{100}{}{You see a greasy, sweating man.}"''
''"{101}{}{You see Eric.}"''
''"{102}{}{You see a greasy, sweating man. He looks quite miserable.}"''

'''Foxes''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] found in [[Appalachia]].

==Characteristics==
===Biology===
Foxes in Appalachia have not undergone any apparent major [[Radiation#Mutations|mutations]], but have suffered from some degree of hair loss. Much like the [[Squirrel (Fallout 76)|squirrel]], their general appearance has remained largely the same as those living prior to the [[Great War]], with only a few minor changes, such as their larger ears.

===Gameplay attributes===
Foxes will not actually attack the player character, they will instead run away when approached. They often stick together in packs.

[[#Scorched frog|Scorched frog]] |location =[[Appalachia]] |affiliation = |actor = |dialogue = }} '''Frogs''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] found in [[Appalachia]]. ==Characteristics== ===Biology=== Usually found near bodies of water, these frogs have mutated from those living prior to the [[Great War]]. The front legs have developed into powerful arms able to lift the body off the ground, rendering the smaller rear legs idle during movement. The long toes of the front arms are tipped with sharp talons. Frogs are marked with a distinct bright-blue glow and occasionally discharge crackling arcs of electricity. The glow is similar to that of [[Nuka-Cola Quantum (Fallout 76)|Nuka-Cola Quantum]], showing similarities to the [[Mirelurk#Nukalurk|Nukalurks]] found at [[Nuka-World (location)|Nuka-World]] in [[the Commonwealth]] and the [[Nuka-Cola plant]] in the [[Capital Wasteland]]. The mouth is filled with numerous small, pointed teeth, and the back is covered in sharp quills. ===Gameplay attributes=== Frogs are non-hostile with very few [[Hit Points]], meaning they can be easily killed. They may drop [[Uranium ore (Fallout 76)|uranium ore]] and [[Glowing blood pack (Fallout 76)|glowing blood packs]]. ==Variants== ===Frog=== A small, standard frog. {{Stats creature FO76|start}} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Frog |form id ={{ID|00110732}} |edid =EncCritterFrog01Template |level =1 |perception =0 |hp =10 |dt =0 |dr =0 |er =0 |rr =0 |pr =0 |xp =2 |aggression =0 |confidence =0 |assistance =2 |attack1 =Melee (0 {{Icon|damage}}) |attack2 =empty |items =* {{Icon|dead}} [[Frog leg]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Frog egg]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Uranium ore (Fallout 76)|Uranium ore]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Glowing blood pack (Fallout 76)|Glowing blood packs]] }} {{Stats creature FO76|end}} ===Scorched frog=== [[File:Scorched Frog.png|thumb]] A frog that has been infected by the [[Scorched Plague]]. {{Stats creature FO76|start}} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Scorched frog |form id ={{ID|003afe1d}} |edid =EncCritterFrog02Scorched |level =1 |perception =0 |hp =10 |dt =0 |dr =0 |er =0 |rr =0 |pr =0 |xp =2 |aggression =0 |confidence =0 |assistance =2 |attack1 =Melee (0 {{Icon|damage}}) |attack2 =empty |items =* {{Icon|dead}} [[Frog leg]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Frog egg]] }} {{Stats creature FO76|end}} ==Locations== * Ten will reliably appear at [[Carleton Mine]] after jumping down into the pool. [[Spin the Wheel]] |affiliation = |actor = |dialogue = }} {{Quotation|The source of endless fireside horror stories, the Grafton Monster is said to be a lumbering, pale, headless horror that wanders the woodlands of Grafton, West Virginia.|[[Fallout 76 loading screens|''Fallout 76'' loading screens]]}} '''Grafton Monsters''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] encountered in [[Appalachia]] {{In|FO76}}. ==Background==
Until the late 21st century, the "Grafton Monster" was largely a mythical creature which drew [[Cryptids|cryptid]] hunters to the namesake town of [[Grafton]], [[Appalachia|West Virginia]]. Around that time, however, myth was made flesh by [[West-Tek]] at their [[West Tek research center (Fallout 76)|research center]] near [[Huntersville]]. Using the '''FEVS-006458''' strain of the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]] in experiments taking place on [[Timeline (2050-2099)#2077|October 23, 2077]], the scientists created a stable, if horrifying, mutation. Derived from the strain that created the mutant beasts known as the [[snallygaster]]s, some engineered tweaks to the genome produced a violent, hulking giant of a mutant that shattered the containment unit, but was otherwise a stable case of FEV transformation (excepting the absence of a discernible head). Once initial studies were over, the newborn "monster" was sedated and loaded up to be transported off-site discreetly.[[West Tek research center terminal entries#Report: Test Subject AM53|West Tek research center terminal entries; advanced mutations lab terminal, Report: Test Subject AM53]] Mid-transport, the outbreak of the [[Great War]] caused the convoy to run off the road after the blinding flash of the bombs disoriented the [[John Bunton|truck driver]], crashing the vehicle and allowing the creature to escape into the wild.[[John Bunton's holotape]]
{{Small|'''Note:''' The holotape's final script notes read ''"A Grafton Monster escapes the back of the truck and runs off."'', confirming that this holotape depicts the Grafton Monster's escape.}} The creatures have since spread across the region.
==Characteristics== Another horrid creation of West-Tek's research into genetic manipulation, the Grafton Monster is headless, hairless and has a grayish color skin with a leathery texture. It stands around 7.5 feet (2.3 meters) tall and has an oversized chest. The mutations that turned it into a powerhouse have also turned its skin and led to the development of glands that can eject globs of corrosive, oily substance in a wide area around it. A large, hulking monster, its size limits its ability to maneuver into tight spaces. It will generally be hostile towards nearby creatures as well as the player character. ===Biology=== The Grafton Monster is a gigantic, hairless gray creature with a disproportionately large upper torso and arms, stumpy legs and enormous three-fingered fists. Its head is non-distinct, seemingly tucked beneath the bulk of its shoulder muscles, which makes it rather difficult to make successful headshots on the creature. It was once human before it was horribly mutated by an experimental FEV strain. ===Gameplay attributes=== A creature that can be quick for its size, it will use its arms as well as its legs to hurl itself towards a target. It can stun the player character for a few seconds. Also, it will launch projectiles (a black liquid) or throw giant rocks similar to super mutant behemoths. [[Spin the Wheel]] |affiliation = |actor = |dialogue = }} The '''gulper''' is a [[Fallout 76 creatures|creature]] found in [[Appalachia]] {{In|FO76}}. ==Background== Gulpers are descendants of pre-War salamanders.''"Sample retrieved from a lagoon west of the Thunder Mountain Power Plant. Appears to be a descendant of the humble salamander.''"
[[Enclave research facility terminal entries#Subject Z-02|Enclave research facility terminal entries; Subject Z-02]] Preferring to stay near water, they can also hang on trees in order to take their victims by surprise, slide through swamp-like areas, and hide underwater. Gulpers can be found throughout [[the Mire]] and the [[Cranberry Bog]]. ==Characteristics== ===Biology=== Their skin is coated in a thin mucus, and their coloration is blotchy and uneven. They stand with a hunched back around six feet tall and walk upright on their hind legs when moving slowly or standing still. They run using all four legs and are able to outrun a non-mutated human. If a player gets too close, they can pounce and swing their massive clawed hands, dealing significant damage. ===Gameplay attributes=== Having movement patterns similar to deathclaws, when engaged in combat, they will rush towards the player, trying to dodge bullets if shot, and will attack with its paws and its large mouth, or even do a slide attack where they hit the player with their snout. Gulpers can also be seen hanging upside down on tree branches, dropping down to attack the player when they come near. Gulpers also have the passive ability of slowly regenerating health. Gulpers will not enter buildings or climb stairs. If a player enters a building or climbs stairs, the gulper will retreat but stay in the general area. ==Variants== {{Stats creature FO76|start}} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Gulper newt |form id [[Dangerous Pastimes]]{{icon|event}} |affiliation = |actor = |dialogue = }} '''Hermit crabs''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] found in [[Appalachia]]. ==Characteristics== Hermit crabs are giant creatures on par with [[Fog crawler (Fallout 76)|fog crawlers]], [[Mirelurk (Fallout 76)|mirelurk queens]] and [[Super mutant (Fallout 76)#Behemoth|super mutant behemoths]], though not quite as tall as the latter. Should something or someone venture close enough, the hermit crab will reveal itself and attack with its massive claws. The process of extracting itself from its shell takes time and should usually suffice to put some distance between the player character and the crab, provided the creature did not get the jump on its prey. Hermit crabs are heavy hitters and can inflict immense damage with their claws while soaking up high amounts of firepower in return. However, these crabs are quite slow and not exactly agile. They don't fit through most doors and cannot mount obstacles. However, they do have the ability to create hatchlings that pour out at their enemy in waves. They will stop, pull halfway back into their shell and begin shaking before releasing between four and six hermit crab hatchlings at a time. Sometimes, they release hatchlings upon death. Hermit crabs usually do not attack until suitable prey gets within four to five yards of their position. They will, however, reveal themselves and actively start searching for trespassers if one stays in the general area for too long. This happens even when the player character remains hidden during this time. ==Variants== ===Hermit crab hatchling=== A newly-hatched hermit crab. {{Stats creature FO76|start}} {{Stats creature [[The Big Bloom]] {{seasonal}} }} '''Honey beasts''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] encountered in [[Appalachia]] {{in|FO76}}. ==Background== The creatures called "honey beasts" are the [[Mutations|mutated]] descendants of ordinary honeybees that were exposed to high levels of [[radiation]] following the [[Great War]]. Honey beasts and their swarms typically reside in the regions of [[the Forest]], [[the Mire]], and the [[Toxic Valley]]. ==Characteristics== ===Biology=== Most honey beasts dwarf the average [[human]] in size and prominently features large beehives on its thorax that ooze honey. Due to its comparatively significant size increase and the resulting mass, the species' wings have become stubby and severely frayed and render it no longer able to fly. As such, mobility is restricted to moving around on the ground, although it can be observed also walking on walls. ===Gameplay attributes=== Honey beasts move slowly, and when engaging with hostiles, they will release [[bee swarm]]s from the hives on their backs causing an easy distraction for the beast to make its attack. They attack slowly but powerfully and can cause immense damage if they manage to lock the player character into a stagger. Fire and cryogenic weapons do not inflict additional damage to the honey beast. ==Variants== ===Honey beast=== [[File:FO76 Honey Beast.png|thumb]] This is the base variant of the honey beast. {{Stats creature FO76|start}} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Honey beast |form id ={{ID|0000e7d7}} |level =16 |perception =8 |family =honeybeast |rr =Immune |pr =100 |aggression =2 |confidence =4 |assistance =1 |items =* {{Icon|dead}} [[Stimpak (Fallout 76)|Stimpak]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Honey]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Honeycomb]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Gold scrap]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Excess adhesive]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Royal jelly (junk)|Royal jelly]] }} {{Stats creature FO76|end}} ===Putrified honey beast=== [[File:Putrified Honey Beast.png|thumb]] A slightly stronger honey beast variant. {{Stats creature FO76|start}} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Putrified honey beast |form id ={{ID|00345a3e}} |level =26 |perception =8 |family =honeybeast |rr =Immune |pr =100 |aggression =2 |confidence =4 |assistance =1 |items =* {{Icon|dead}} [[Stimpak (Fallout 76)|Stimpak]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Honey]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Honeycomb]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Gold scrap]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Excess adhesive]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Royal jelly (junk)|Royal jelly]] }} {{Stats creature FO76|end}} ===Raging honey beast=== [[File:Raging Honey Beast.png|thumb]] An even stronger honey beast variant. {{Stats creature FO76|start}} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Raging honey beast |form id ={{ID|00345a42}} |level =36 |perception =8 |family =honeybeast |rr =Immune |pr =100 |aggression =2 |confidence =4 |assistance =1 |items =* {{Icon|dead}} [[Stimpak (Fallout 76)|Stimpak]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Honey]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Honeycomb]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Gold scrap]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Excess adhesive]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Royal jelly (junk)|Royal jelly]] }} {{Stats creature FO76|end}} ===Glowing honey beast=== [[File:Glowing Honey Beast.png|thumb]] A more powerful variant, the glowing honey beast is a honey beast that glows green. {{icon|FOT}} [[The Belt]] }} '''Iguanas''' are large, herbivorous lizards originally native to Central and South America, which proliferated across North America in the wake of the [[Great War]]. They are a staple of the [[Fallout series|''Fallout'' series]], found in almost every game as a meal, and included in ''[[The Vault Dweller's Official Cookbook]]''.''[[The Vault Dweller's Official Cookbook]]'', p. 29 ==Background== Found across the wasteland from [[New California]][[Iguana-on-a-stick (Fallout)]] and the [[Mojave Wasteland]][[Iguana-on-a-stick (Fallout: New Vegas)]] to [[Appalachia]],[[Iguana on a stick (Fallout 76)]] the [[Capital Wasteland]],[[Iguana-on-a-stick (Fallout 3)]] and [[the Commonwealth]],[[Iguana on a stick (Fallout 4)]] iguanas are a common source of meat to wastelanders, and are even kept as pets.COMBATAI.MSG: ''"{2550}{}{I'm gonna feed you to my pet iguana}"''
'''Note''': Used in ''Fallout'' ([[COMBATAI.MSG (Fallout)|COMBATAI.MSG]]) and ''Fallout 2'' ([[COMBATAI.MSG (Fallout 2)|COMBATAI.MSG]]) as a generic combat float. Iguanas have a common defense mechanism, shedding their tail as a distraction,[[Pioneer Scout Badge Exam answers#Herpetologist|Pioneer Scout Badge Exam answers]]:
Question: ''"Your pet iguana is being threatened by the family dog. What would be a common defense mechanism employed by the iguana?"''
Correct answer: ''"Shed its own tail as a distraction"'' but it does not stop larger predators who prey on the common lizard.The [[Vault Dweller]]: ''"{122}{}{Who's Victor?}"''
[[Sherry]]: ''"{125}{}{Victor's right over there. He's the meanest of us all. He likes torturing iguanas that he catches. I don't really like him, to tell the truth, but he's one of us.}"''
([[SHERRY.MSG|Sherry's dialogue]]) It is unknown just how the lizard became so commonplace,[[Underworld resident]]: ''"Greta, can I get some food over here?"''
[[Greta]]: ''"What do you want?"''
Underworld resident: ''"You ever wonder where all those iguanas come from? I do. I guess it don't matter, 'cause they sure are tasty. You got any?"''
Greta: ''"I can go find out for you."''
Underworld resident: ''"I'll try not to starve before you get back."''
([[Underworld conversations]]; [[UnderworldGhoul01.txt|Underworld resistdent]] and [[Greta.txt|Greta's dialogue]]) but they are so ubiquitous that they can form the basis of nutrition for impoverished groups.[[Caleb Smith]]: ''"Can we have something other than iguana tonight? Anything?"''
([[CalebSmith.txt|Caleb Smith's dialogue]]) However, it is popular with all classes of society,[[Fallout endings#Gizmo takes control|''Fallout'' endings]]: ''"Junktown becomes the new boomtown under the careful, and profitable, guidance of Don Gizmo. He profits the most, and continues to increase the size of his casino, and the scope of his power, until he chokes to death while eating some Iguana-on-a-stick."'' as iguana meat is readily available. Though stringy, it can be prepared in a variety of ways: Simple [[iguana bits]] can be served as skewers with vegetables,PRO ITEM.MSG: ''"{10300}{}{Iguana-on-a-stick}"''
''"{10301}{}{Some charred meat and vegetables on a cooking stick.}"''
'''Note''': Present in both ''Fallout'' ([[PRO ITEM.MSG (Fallout)|PRO ITEM.MSG]]) and ''Fallout 2'' ([[PRO ITEM.MSG (Fallout 2)|PRO ITEM.MSG]]).[[Zimmer]]: ''"Did I order already? If I didn't, I'd like Iguana Bits with vegetables."''
[[Mister Buckingham]]: ''"Your food will be ready shortly, Mister Zimmer."''
([[Rivet City conversations]]; [[Zimmer.txt|Zimmer]] and [[RCMisterBuckingham.txt|Mister Buckingham's dialogue]]) as a sandwich,The [[Lone Wanderer]]: ''"Tell me about Allistair Tenpenny."''
[[Margaret Primrose]]: ''"Every day it's the same thing. The man has no imagination with his meals. {{Tooltip|But it's his building, so everyday I make that damned 'Iguana Bits sandwich, no salt, with a peeled pear on the side. Send it up to the penthouse.'|teasingly mocking}}"''
([[MargaretPrimrose.txt|Margaret Primrose's dialogue]]) or even as [[iguana soup]].[[Iguana soup (Fallout 4)]] and [[Iguana soup (Fallout 76)]] It can also be roasted whole in its skin, becoming an [[iguana-on-a-stick]],PRO ITEM.MSG: ''"{8100}{}{Iguana-on-a-stick}"''
''"{8101}{}{A cooked iguana, roasted in it's own skin.}"''
'''Note''': Present in both ''Fallout'' ([[PRO ITEM.MSG (Fallout)|PRO ITEM.MSG]]) and ''Fallout 2'' ([[PRO ITEM.MSG (Fallout 2)|PRO ITEM.MSG]]). and even oven baked.[[Gary Staley]]: ''"Make sure to clean all the empty tables."''
[[Angela Staley]]: ''"Okay. Don't forget to check the oven. Nobody will eat a burnt iguana."''
([[Rivet City conversations]]; [[GaryStaley.txt|Gary Staley]] and [[AngelaStaley.txt|Angela Staley's dialogue]]) Talented cooks can turn it into other dishes, such as savory iguana sausages, served to the [[New Vegas Strip]] visitors at [[Vault 21]].[[Vault 21 terminal entries#Diner Menu|Vault 21 terminal entries; Vault 21 guest terminal, Diner Menu]] Iguana meat seems to go well with mustard and onions.[[Mikey Frazier]]: ''"{110}{}{There's mustard and onions over there.}"''
([[Scmikey.msg|Mikey Frazier's dialogue]]) Talented cooks can count on steady income, as good iguana meals tend to be very popular. Perhaps the most popular of these cooks was [[Iguana Bob Frazier]] of [[the Hub]] around 2161, who became a staple of the Merchant Market, offering freshly roasted iguana[[PRO SCEN.MSG (Fallout)]]: ''"{16500}{}{Iguana Stand}"''
''"{16501}{}{The home of Bob's Iguana Bits. What's not to love about fresh-roasted iguana?}"'' and "prime cut" iguana bits. The latter were especially popular in the Hub,The [[Vault Dweller]]: ''"{1056}{}{Iguana}"''
[[Butch Harris]]: ''"{1133}{butch108}{Now there's some good eating. Bob's has got the best charred iguana this side of the desert.}"''
([[BUTCH.MSG|Butch Harris' dialogue]])[[Far Go Traders guard]]: ''"{106}{}{Hmm, I've a craving for some iguana on a stick.}"''
([[FGTGARD.MSG|Far Go Traders guards' dialogue]])[[Luke (Fallout)|Luke]] and [[Mat]]: ''"{119}{}{I'm heading strait for Bobs!}"''
([[HGENCVAN.MSG|Luke and Mat's dialogue]]) though they were not made from actual iguanas, but human meat sourced from [[Morbid|Doc Morbid]] of [[Junktown]].''[[Blackmail Iguana Bob]]'' The secret never got out, and the Fraziers continued their business, with Bob's sharply-dressed[[Mikey Frazier]]'s character description: ''"{100}{}{You see a sharp-dressed guy hawking lizard kebabs.}"''
([[Scmikey.msg|Mikey Frazier's dialogue]]) son operating the [[Son of Bob's Iguana Bits]] franchise at the NCR capital in 2241.[[Mikey Frazier]]'s character description: ''"{102}{}{For a lizard-on-a-stick vendor, this guy's got style. He's clean, well-dressed and runs a pretty spotless little operation.}"''
([[Scmikey.msg|Mikey Frazier's dialogue]]) On the other side of the continent, [[Gary Staley]] of [[Rivet City]] around 2277 specialized in [[mirelurk]] cakes, but his iguana was very popular, either whole or served as bits.[[Gary Staley]]: ''"Let me introduce myself. I am Gary Staley gourmet chef and gourmand. I'll be preparing your meal. My specialty is Mirelurk Cakes. Although the iguana is very popular too."''
([[GaryStaley.txt|Gary Staley's dialogue]]) [[Margaret Primrose]] was also good with iguana, and served [[Allistair Tenpenny]] his favorite iguana sandwich every day. ==Characteristics== For such a commonplace creature, the iguanas are yet to appear in living form in the game. Deathclaws, such as [[Valdis]], can be insulted by comparing them to iguanas, but they are not derived from the lizard.The [[Chosen One]]: ''"{110}{}{No offense to your fellow deathclaws, but you sound more... educated, shall we say?}"''
[[Valdis]]: "''{131}{}{Yes. We are quite diverse in our levels of education. I am doing my best to continue mine in my spare time.}"''
The Chosen One: ''"{132}{}{An iguana with a goal. How freaking cute.}"''
([[Ocvaldis.msg|Valdis' dialogue]]) Aside from the odd mention, iguanas appear primarily as various meals throughout the [[Capital Wasteland|Capital]] and [[Mojave Wasteland]]s, [[New California]], [[Appalachia]] as well as [[the Commonwealth]]. The aforementioned [[Iguana Bob Frazier|Iguana Bob]] {{in|FO1}} is notable for being involved in a cannibal scheme, where actual roasted iguanas are served alongside skewers made from human bits. ==Appearances== Iguanas appear {{In|FO1}}, {{In|FO2|noin}}, {{In|FO3|noin}}, {{In|FNV|noin}}, {{In|FO4|noin}}, {{In|FO76|noin}}, {{In|FOT|noin}}, and {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Behind the scenes== * In ''Fallout'' and ''Fallout 2'', the combat float ''"I'm gonna feed you to my pet iguana"'' suggests that knowledge of iguanas being herbivorous is not that common. You seen that thing?"'' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] found in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background==
Before the [[Great War]], [[Isaac Garrahan]] owned several sloths at his family's [[Garrahan Estate|estate]]. They are recorded to have escaped the enclosure on at least two occasions, and the lack of sloth remains in the cages at the [[Garrahan Estate]] implies they escaped again following the War.[[Isaac's message to the Sloth]][[Garrahan Estate terminal entries#Log 08-22-77|Garrahan Estate terminal entries; Log 08-22-77]] The mega sloths are three-toed sloths mutated by [[radiation]]. Standing much taller than the average human, their body is covered with filthy and shaggy fur with clusters of mushrooms growing in the fur on their back, similar to fungus grew in the fur of pre-War sloths.[https://modiphius.net/en-us/collections/fallout-wasteland-warfare/products/fallout-miniatures-cryptids-megasloth Fallout: Miniatures - Cryptids - Megasloth]: ''"These gentle giants are the descendants of sloths. Slow and calm, they spend their days eating leaves and hanging from trees sturdy enough to hold them. Their thick fur is an ecosystem all on its own, supporting an interesting variety of insects and plants. Chief amongst these are the mushrooms that sprout over its body, a fungus that has a symbiotic relationship with the sloths. It is rumoured these creatures first arrived in the USA before the Great War as pets, though as war broke out they escaped before finally mutating into the creatures seen now. Despite their docile nature, they are powerful combatants able to fight head on with yao guai and come out victorious."'' These [[megasloth mushroom]]s release clouds of spores when the sloth shakes its body, deterring aggressors that get too close. They have heavily calloused patches of skin and sharp teeth. Mega sloths are much larger than pre-War variants.
==Gameplay attributes== Unlike most creatures, mega sloths may not be immediately hostile; they will ignore anything that is not attacking them. Mega sloths can be found throughout [[the Mire]] and [[Cranberry Bog]]. Some can be found dangling from large trees, similar to [[Gulper (Fallout 76)|gulpers]]. In close combat, they can use their claws to scratch, dealing heavy damage. From afar, they may hurl rocks or shake to release a cloud of fungal spores from the mushrooms growing on their back, which clouds one's vision. ==Variants== ===Mega sloth=== {{Stats creature [[Swarm of Suitors]] }}{{For|a cross-game overview|mirelurk}} '''Mirelurks''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures#Mirelurks|creatures]] found in [[Appalachia]]. ==Characteristics== ===Biology=== While usually being associated with mutated crabs, the term mirelurk refers to a range of mutated aquatic species. The crab-like mirelurk is considered both fearsome and formidable by wastelanders. Mirelurks are generally social with others of their kind, although they tend to be aggressive to other creatures and one another if one gets too close to another.[[Mirelurk research]]: ''"The Mirelurk appears to be a fearsome and formidable creature. They are generally social with other mirelurks however they tend to be aggressive to other creatures and one another if one gets too close to another."'' Most adult mirelurks appear to have a hardened carapace on their backs, which is suggested to be their primary defense mechanism. While their eyesight appears to be poor, mirelurks have an extraordinary sense of smell. After using their crab/spider-like legs and large claws to reach and catch prey, they use a smaller set of abdomen claws to strip their prey down to the bone within minutes. Most mirelurks grow remarkably fast, and the shelled-variant has been observed to reach maturity within weeks.[[Mirelurk research]]: ''"Their eye sight appears to be good, but they have an extraordinary sense of smell... their large set of claws appear to be used primarily for hunting. Once their prey been captured the smaller set of claws on their abdomen is used to strip their prey down to the bone in a matter of minutes... the large hardened carapace on their back appears to be their primary defense mechanism... they grow remarkably fast, it only appears to take them a few weeks to reach maturity."'' ===Gameplay attributes=== The mirelurk crab attacks exclusively with melee. They will get close, usually in a group of three or more and attempt to hit the player character with their large claws. They will duck into their hard shell as a way to block incoming melee damage. They do this often and it can become an issue if the player character is being attacked from multiple sides, as when they turn to attack a different foe, the crouched mirelurk will leap up and attack almost instantly. She will attack with powerful melee strikes, and a very effective poison spit attack, which can blanket an entire area in a matter of seconds. This creates an area of effect pool, which ramps up damage the longer the target stays inside. She can also surprise unsuspecting player characters when she rises from a nearby water source other mirelurk are gathered around, but the roar she makes to alert them of her appearance can send them into a panicked run to get away once they hear it. They can also release mirelurk spawn like grenades, using them as a distraction while she kills the opponent. Being one of the few boss enemies, she is very difficult to kill. [[Butcher's Bounty]] }}{{for|a cross-game overview|Mole rat}} '''Mole rats''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] found in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== Mole rats are mutated ''[[Wikipedia:Heterocephalus glaber|Heterocephalus glaber]]'',[[Vault 96 terminal entries#V03-901-1002|Vault 96 terminal entries; biology workstation, V03-901-1002]] or naked mole-rats, that are much larger than their pre-war counterparts. The mole rat is not native to North America, being endemic to Africa, and it is unknown why they began to appear in Appalachia. They have survived as a species by burrowing underground where the soil protected them from direct nuclear explosions. However, they still were greatly mutated by the subsequent fallout, increasing their size as well as their viciousness. A few people in the wastes have even been known to train and keep them as pets. ==Characteristics== ===Biology=== Mole rats grow to the size of a large [[Dog (Fallout 76)|dog]]. They have a naked, pink appearance, with large front teeth and small eyes. They are highly territorial and will attack anything entering their territory. They are surprisingly fast and will attack with a jumping lunge. They are susceptible to the [[Scorched Plague]].[[Ella Ames' bunker terminal entries#Group Recognition.3F|Ella Ames' bunker terminal entries; Ella's terminal, Group Recognition?]] The female brood mothers are larger individuals. ===Gameplay attributes=== Mole rats will tunnel underground to avoid their enemy or close in to attack unseen. They will also retreat to a tunnel if the player character moves to an area that is inaccessible to them, such as on top of a car. This makes them highly difficult to keep track of in groups. This ability is shared with [[Radscorpion (Fallout 76)|radscorpions]] and the [[Mothman]]. If the player character uses a weapon dealing damage over time on a mole rat just as they burrow they can die underground and the corpse will be irretrievable. Mole rats are common pests in the wasteland, but compared to many other enemies mole rats are generally weak. If allowed to swarm, they may become a problem since they have the ability to easily hide from the player character's sight and attack from behind. ==Variants== ===Mole rat=== {{Stats creature [[Tea Time]] |affiliation = |actor = |dialogue = }} '''Mongrels''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] found in [[Appalachia]]. ==Characteristics== Mongrels are commonly found throughout the region. They are aggressive and will hunt anything nearby. They will only perform standard bite and claw attacks. Usually traveling in a group, they will attack from all directions. ==Biology== Mongrels are post-War mutations of canines. They have suffered the common effect of severe loss of fur and a leaner form, to the point of being skeletal in some parts of their body. '''Opossums''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] found in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
Opossums are the mutated descendants of the pre-[[Great War|War]] North American opossum, found throughout Appalachia.<ref>[[Enclave research facility terminal entries#Subject C-02|Enclave research facility terminal entries; Subject C-02]]</ref>

==Characteristics==
Opossums have appendages sprouting from their back, two tails, and multiple heads. The placement of their heads vary. The creatures offer a small amount of experience when killed and flee from the player character if they are approached. They will drop [[opossum meat]] when killed.

==Locations==
* Four will always appear east of [[White Powder Winter Sports]], on a cliff, in a clearing.
* Two will always appear outside of the [[Flatwoods Tavern|tavern]] in [[Flatwoods]].
* One will always appear outside [[Green Country Lodge]].
* May spawn at the unmarked [[sludge trailer]], north of the [[Red Rocket filling station]].
* Deceased opossums are located in the [[Enclave research facility]] holding cell C02.
* Two spawn at [[East Mountain lookout]].

==Appearances==
Opossums appear {{In|FO76}} and {{In|FWW|noin}}.

'''Owlet''' is a [[Fallout 76 creatures#Animals|creature]] in [[Appalachia]].

==Background==
Owlets are juvenile [[Owl|owls]] which have been rendered nearly featherless by mutation following [[radiation]] exposure. They are flightless but have adapted to this by living in caves and can quickly hop along the ground to escape predators.

==Gameplay attributes==
Owlets are non-hostile creatures and will always flee combat. They drop [[owlet meat]] upon death, which may be increased with [[Butcher's Bounty]]. They have 5 [[Damage Resistance]], [[Energy Resistance]], [[Radiation Resistance]], [[Poison Resistance]], [[Fire Resistance]] and [[Cryo Resistance]].

==Locations==
* One can be found within the caverns of [[the Deep]], in proximity to the cave entrance adjacent to [[the Pigsty]]. 
** Due to spawning near [[Cave cricket (Fallout 76)|cave crickets]], the owlet may die. For information on how to encounter the owlet alive, see [[#Notes|notes]].
* One can be found in [[Grahm]]'s cooking pot during the [[Grahm's Meat-Cook]] event.
* One can be found in a containment unit inside the [[Enclave research facility]].
* One can be found on the roof of the classroom at [[Haven Church]].

==Notes==
* Looting the [[owlet meat]] for the first time will automatically unlock the [[owlet nuggets]] recipe. No notification will be displayed.
* In order to observe the owlet alive in the Deep, a player will need to change servers until the owlet and the crickets spawn on opposite ends of the small cave tunnel. Alternatively, the owlet may be encountered more reliably in coordination with a second player. The first player must kill the cave crickets and stay within the area. After a period of approximately 30 minutes, a second player may enter the Deep, causing the actors to respawn. The first player may then eliminate the cave crickets before they can harm the owlet.
* The addition of the owlet spawn on the rooftop of Haven Church, makes the need for the relatively slow method of attempting to find a living specimen in the Deep no longer necessary to acquire the owlet nuggets recipe.  
* It is possible owlets are in reality mutated [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burrowing_owl burrowing owls]. This notion is possibly indicated by the presence of one within [[the Deep]], along with their general appearance and behavior.  

==Appearances==
Owlets were originally cut from {{In|FO76|noin}}, but were introduced in the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. They also appear {{In|FWW}}.

==Behind the scenes==
* Owlets do not have any attacks, however a leftover developer note references an ''"In Place Jump Foot Punch Attack"''.<ref>[https://nukacrypt.com/database/json/0007A2C8 <OwlRace>(0007A2C8)]</ref>
* The owlet at Haven Church was added in [[Fallout 76 patches|patch 29]] by [[Steve Massey]] at the request of players in the BGS Discord.<ref>BGS_Steve (Steve Massey) [[File:FO76 BGS Steve Owlet.png|1px]][[:File:FO76 BGS Steve Owlet.png|on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord]]</ref>

'''Radhogs''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] encountered in the [[Burning Springs (region)|Burning Springs]] region of [[Appalachia]] {{In|FO76BS}}.

==Background==
{{main|hog}}
The radhog is the mutated descendant of pre-War [[Hog|swine]] commonly found in the [[Burning Springs (region)|Burning Springs]] region of [[Ohio]]. Before the [[Great War]], feral pigs were considered an invasive species in Appalachia.<ref>[[Pioneer Scout camp terminal entries#Hunter|Pioneer Scout camp terminal entries; Pioneer badge exam terminal, Tadpole Exams, Hunter]] {{Small|'''Note:''' The correct answer to the question "The government in Charleston decides it's open season to hunt feral pigs in Appalachia. This is because they are what kind of species here?" is "Invasive."}}</ref>

==Characteristics==
===Biology===
Radhogs are heavy-set creatures who appear to have taken on [[radiation]] and various [[mutations]]. Although they retain the general shape of their pre-War variants, radhogs are slightly larger and have much more sickly appearances. They have bulbous, bloodshot eyes, overgrown teeth, two tails, and numerous skin growths. Their stomachs are bulging and rough, and a green and brown discoloration covers the majority of their lower body, spanning from their head to their tails. Patches of hair cover their lower half, mainly around their legs and throat. Some radhogs are seen to have wiry black manes and hog rings on their nose.

The radiation from the fallout has caused them to grow to a great size and gain a far fiercer disposition, making them high ranking predators among the wasteland. ==Characteristics== ===Biology=== Radscorpions sport highly venomous stingers, the ability to burrow underground in seconds, powerful claws, and durable exoskeletons. ===Gameplay attributes=== Radscorpions are fast runners, extremely aggressive, extraordinarily well armored and will use their powerful claws and poisoned tails to attack enemies quickly and relentlessly; capable of dealing a large amount of physical and poison damage in only a few hits. With their ability to burrow underground and traverse large distances seemingly instantaneously, retreating from an encounter is often impossible. Their only weak spot is their relatively small face. Due to their claw and poisonous sting attacks as well as their great maneuverability, radscorpions are powerful melee fighters. If attacked from afar, they will immediately burrow and emerge close to the player character, often in melee range, provided the ground type can be navigated through by them. ==Variants== Because of this, radstags, like [[Brahmin (Fallout 76)|brahmin]], have two heads, less fur and are sometimes covered in cysts. ==Characteristics== ===Biology=== Radstags are descended from deer that survived the Great War, resulting in mutations such as bicephaly and the presence of a third pair of atrophied legs. These two smaller legs hang from the upper part of the chest. When they feel safe, they can be seen drinking from water sources, pasture grass or bushes or resting while lying on the ground. ===Gameplay attributes=== Most radstags will flee on instinct when the player character or a predator approaches too close or attacks. However, some variants escape this rule and can attack their opponents with hooves or headbutts. ==Variants== ===Radstag yearling=== A juvenile variant of radstag. They are easily identifiable by their small size and their brownish coat peppered with small white spots. They will flee instinctively from the player character. They maintain four strong primary legs, but have also grown a thin set of arm-like limbs protruding from the sides of the jaw. Radtoads possess ferocious pointed teeth and a long, tri-barbed tongue. Numerous yellow-red eyes are scattered about the head, and clusters of eggs are strewn about the back. ===Gameplay attributes=== Radtoads use their long tongue to hit targets at a distance, choosing to attack with jagged teeth up close. Most radtoads can also release a cluster of eggs that act as mines. If a target tramples the cluster, the pile will burst, inflicting damage.[[Fallout 76 loading screens]]: ''"Radtoads use their elongated tongues to ambush prey at a distance. [[#Nuclear Winter|Extra crispy scorchbeast]] {{Icon|FO76NW}} |actor = |dialogue = }}{{for|the boss enemy|Scorchbeast queen}} '''Scorchbeasts''', also known by the code name '''Sierra Bravo''' by the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]], are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] found in [[Appalachia]] and major enemies {{in|FO76}}. ==Background== The first scorchbeast was accidentally created when [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]] scientists exposed irradiated bats to biochemical experiments. Despite concerns and suggestions of destroying the creatures, [[Thomas Eckhart|Secretary Eckhart]] ordered further study of the creature at the [[glassed cavern]], an old [[Atomic Mining Services|AMS]] mining complex, while keeping the officer corps largely uninformed.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#5.4.8|Whitespring surveillance recording; 5.4.8]][[Brotherhood transponders#Brotherhood transponder EL-7B|Brotherhood transponders; EL-7B]] The future president wished to convince monitoring systems that they were an immediate threat, raising the alert level to [[DEFCON]] 1 and giving him access to the nuclear arsenal. Although kept in isolation, theoretically, individual beasts made it to the surface at regular intervals, as early as 2084.[[Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries#Some Kind of Bat|Sam Blackwell's bunker terminal entries; Some Kind of Bat]] Despite increasing opposition from the officer corps, Eckhart unleashed them upon the region in early 2085, unintentionally releasing a pestilence that threatened to render the human race extinct on a continental scale.[[Whitespring surveillance recordings#8.5.2|Whitespring surveillance recording; 8.5.2.]] The people of the [[Appalachia]]n wasteland first learned about the scorchbeasts from reports issued by the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood of Steel]] under [[Elizabeth Taggerdy|Paladin Taggerdy]], who referred to the creatures under the code name "Sierra Bravo." Although they dismissed them as pure stories to give Taggerdy an excuse to commandeer ammo and supplies, they were soon proven wrong by their appearance and the plague that followed in their wake. The [[Scorched]], mutated creatures created out of [[human]]s afflicted by the [[Scorched Plague]], became an existential threat to the people of Appalachia.[[Morgantown Airport terminal entries#Scorched Research|Morgantown Airport terminal entries; Responders laboratory terminal, scorched research]] The situation was made worse by their expansive breeding limited only by the available nest space in the mining tunnels below [[State#West Virginia|West Virginia]].[[Fort Defiance terminal entries#Paladin Taggerdy's terminal|Fort Defiance terminal entries; Paladin Taggerdy's terminal, scorchbeast analysis]] Scorchbeasts also started [[Scorchbeast nest|nesting]] in [[Watoga]]. [[File:FO76 Glassed cavern (Battle area).png|thumb|right|240x240px|An alpha scorchbeast slain during the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|Brotherhood]]'s failed Operation Touchdown in the [[glassed cavern]]]] Since then, the scorchbeasts became an established threat beneath the entirety of Appalachia. They regularly dug to the surface, destroying settlements and devouring humans, leaving [[Fissure site|large rifts]] in the landscape. The only way to safely close the rifts was to launch [[Nuclear missile (Fallout 76)|nuclear missiles]] from one of three [[Appalachian Automated Launch System|automated silos]] scattered across Appalachia, collapsing the rifts and killing those scorchbeasts that remain. None of the factions in Appalachia managed to achieve this feat, either due to a lack of means ([[Responders]] and [[Free States]]) or ideological opposition to the use of nuclear weapons (Brotherhood of Steel). Only the [[Vault 76]] [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Dwellers]], entering Appalachia after the humans had been wiped out or had left the area, managed to push back the scorchbeasts and destroy them in nuclear attrition, preventing an extinction-level event.[https://youtu.be/gi8PTAJ2Hjs?t=28m16s The Making of Fallout 76 - Noclip Documentary] Scorchbeasts are partially responsible for the creation of the Scorched, as according to research by the [[Vault 76 overseer]], their underground colony contains a virus responsible for the Scorched Plague, causing the crystalline growths seen on the Scorched.[[Overseer's log - Morgantown]] ===Biology=== Thought to be derived from a species of pygmy bats, scorchbeast are the apex predators of [[Appalachia]].''"The Scorchbeasts have definitely won the title of apex predator in Appalachia. There's no doubt they've evolved from some species of bat which makes them quite fascinating creatures due to their size. I'd like to think it was one of those cute pygmy bats we used to chase out of the caves when I was little... Daddy always said they'd have their revenge!"''
([[Ella Ames' bunker terminal entries#Scorchbeasts|Ella Ames' bunker terminal entries; Ella's terminal, Scorchbeasts:]]) The creature has retained its ancestors' pointed ears, membranous wings, and echolocation. However, it has lost most of its fur, grown to a tremendous size, developed an extra pair of functional legs, and evolved to become the carrier of a plague which converts any infected living being into the Scorched. Despite their size, scorchbeasts possess considerable agility, and even when grounded they can leap several times their body length in one bound. Despite the behavior of their progenitors, scorchbeasts are not averse to daytime hunting and are known to cooperatively hunt in groups. Strong and aggressive, it attacks with razor-sharp teeth and claws. The beasts are potent foes, as lamented by the [[Responders]], whose anti-scorchbeast tactics boil down to doing everything in their power to keep away from it and finding an enclosed space to fire from, as scorchbeasts are simply too big to fit into small spaces. Scorchbeasts also emit radiation and are capable of using powerful ultrasonic echolocation as a means of navigating or commanding their Scorched servants on the ground.[[Sensor module specs]] In addition to this, they possess the ability to emit a powerful sonic blast capable of shattering wood and metal structures from their mouths much like [[Mirelurk (Fallout 76)|mirelurk kings]] and [[Mothman|mothmen]], but on a far larger scale. Their other nonconventional attack includes flying over an area and saturating it with an acidic, radioactive mist that permeates through cover. ==Characteristics== [[File:Fallout 76 Scorchbeast sonic attack 1.png|thumb|right|240x240px|Sonic attacks deal area of effect explosive damage]] Scorchbeasts, detectable by the distinct sound of their wings when they are flying overhead, are generally hostile to the player character and will summon additional Scorched enemies while fighting. They utilize three different attacks, the first being a long-range sonic attack, which is performed while flying and counts as explosive damage rather than energy damage. The interval between these attacks is at least ten seconds.[[Fallout 76 patch 1.0.6.0]] The second attack is a radioactive fog, commonly referred to as crop dusting due to its dispersing from its wings much like a crop duster, and capable of traveling through roofs and walls. The scorchbeast will continue to dust an area, even if one is hidden. The scorchbeast queen uses a variant of this attack that deals poison damage, rather than the standard radiation damage. The third attack style is a sweeping attack which it utilizes while on the ground, using its wings to swing at its enemies within melee range to deliver heavy damage to them. They can also perform a lunging attack to force enemies to turn around to resume attacking it if it lunges over them and gets behind them. Their final attack consists of a shockwave attack that can not only damage enemies, but also summon Scorched to its aid to take out its would-be killers. A diseased scorchbeast may inflict [[the Blight]], a [[Fallout 76 diseases|disease]] which lowers all [[Fallout 76 SPECIAL|SPECIAL]] stats by 1 point, randomly upon landing any attack, including their sonic blasts. The scorchbeast heals itself over time similar to other [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]]. They have also been seen to attack and infect other enemies during combat. Their attacks can be subverted by fleeing or sheltering in a small structure, or utilizing [[automated surface to air missile]] batteries. Crippling either of a scorchbeast's wings will force it to land, after finding a suitable spot. The landing behavior can be interrupted by stagger effects applied by perks like [[Tank Killer]] or [[One Gun Army]]. Attacking the head of a scorchbeast will deal 150% damage. Almost all scorchbeast attacks create and are considered explosions, and will be mitigated by a [[Dense|dense torso mod]] or the [[Hardy]] perk. Upon entering combat, a scorchbeast will summon a wave of [[Scorched]] minions. Though they're very aggressive, Scorchbeasts may rarely be non-hostile to players. There are several non-hostile scorchbeasts found in certain areas, but there is a small chance for any other scorchbeasts that appear to be non-hostile until attacked. ==Variants== {{Stats creature FO76|start}} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Scorchbeast |form id ={{ID|00011c80}} |edid = EncScorchbeast01Template |level =50 |perception =7 |family =scorchbeast |rr =Immune |pr =0 |aggression =1 |confidence =4 |assistance =0 |items = }} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Scorchbeast |form id ={{ID|003c2bd4}} |edid =EncScorchbeast02 |level =65 |perception =7 |family =scorchbeast |rr =Immune |pr =0 |aggression =1 |confidence =4 |assistance =0 |items = }} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Scorchbeast |form id ={{ID|003c2b4f}} |edid =EncScorchbeast03 |level =80 |perception =7 |family =scorchbeast |rr =Immune |pr =0 |aggression =1 |confidence =4 |assistance =0 |items = }} {{Stats creature FO76|end}} ===''Nuclear Winter''=== The extra crispy scorchbeast was encountered in ''[[Nuclear Winter (mode)|Nuclear Winter]]'' as a late-game creature that posed a high-risk, high-reward challenge. |} ==Notes== [[File:Scorchbeast queen.jpg|thumb|right|300px| ]] * The [[Fallout 76 diseases|diseased]] Scorchbeast queen will inflict the [[Fallout 76 diseases|Blight]], which reduces all [[Fallout 76 SPECIAL|SPECIAL]] stats by 1. This may be triggered by any of its attacks in relation to the player character's [[Endurance (Fallout 76)|Endurance]] and [[Disease Resistance]]. * The scorchbeast queen is the first biological non-humanoid being to be considered a major antagonist. * If any non-[[Scorched Plague|Scorched]] hostiles are present around the event arena, the queen may wander off and attack them instead of the party. If the enemy is unable to be Scorched, the hostiles must be dealt with in order to regain the queen's aggro. * The scorchbeast queen cannot be disintegrated into ash or goo. * Unless grounded via cripple, the queen will not land unless it has opportunity to deal melee attacks. If the party is situated on objects it may not reach, it will not land. Examples include, but are not limited to: ** [[Drop Site V9]] - most parts of the fence or bunker; the atop or inside the barn with the elevator lift from [[glassed cavern]]. ** [[Forward Station Delta]] - inside the encampment, or upon its catwalks. ** [[Fissure site Prime]] - atop dilapidated buildings. ** [[Overgrown sundew grove]] - inside the grove or atop the mutated sundew plants; within/atop the barn near V9. ** [[Glassed cavern]] - upon or inside either AMS structure. ** Upon placed [[Survival tent]]s or stacked [[power armor chassis]]; especially floating tents. *The scorchbeast queen has a number of weaknesses: ** Affected by both [[Fallout 76 legendary effects|Hunter's]] and [[Fallout 76 legendary effects|Zealot's]] gear. ** Crippling one of the queen's wings will force it to land, after finding a suitable spot. The landing behavior can be interrupted by stagger effects applied by perks like [[Tank Killer]] or [[One Gun Army]]. ** Attacking the head will deal 150% damage. ** Due to her large hitbox, some explosions may not connect properly if unless precisely placed. To deal optimal damage, explosions should connect with its underbelly while it is grounded. ** The scorchbeast queen will cease attacking momentarily while hovering over an area it is trying to land in. The cue for this is its behavior of floating largely in place, rather than strafing. Attacking and inflicting a [[stagger]] will interrupt the animation and prevent the landing. ** Barring the radiation hazards, all of the queen's attacks are considered explosions and will be mitigated by the [[Hardy]] perk or a [[padded]]/[[Dense|dense torso mod]]. *** Its grounded melee attacks are considered both melee and explosion, so [[Blocker]] and Fireproof may be used in tandem. ==Appearances== The Scorchbeast queen appears only {{In|FO76}}. ==Behind the scenes== * The existence of the scorchbeast queen was a secret kept by Bethesda as promotional materials did not advertise the boss fight. She was discovered a day after the game was released when a party member nuked the specific fissure site by chance. It took the party about twenty minutes to kill her.[https://www.vgr.com/fallout-76-scorchbeast-queen-boss/ VGR: Fallout 76 Players Discover Scorchbeast Queen End-Game Boss] * The rarest drops from the scorchbeast queen are the [[Plan: Ultracite calibrated shocks]], [[Plan: Ultracite targeting HUD]], [[Plan: Ultracite Tesla coils]] and [[Plan: Ultracite reactive plates]], each at a 0.08% drop rate. * The [[Fallout 76 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide|Fallout 76 game guide]] states that the scorchbeast queen deals "cold" attacks, which implies cryo damage. Although her attacks have off-white VFX, they deal energy damage. ==Bugs== * {{platforms|pc,xboxone,ps4}} The scorchbeast queen may occasionally wander out of bounds, making the fight impossible if it strays too far.{{verify|verified}} * {{platforms|pc,xboxone,ps4}} If killed near the edge of the game world, the scorchbeast queen may fall out-of-bounds and be rendered unlootable.{{verify|verified}} * {{platforms|pc,xboxone,ps4}} A known-bug with [[Heart of the Enemy]], fast traveling may cause the body of the queen to teleport behind you after arriving at your destination. This may be exploited as a workaround for the above bug.{{verify|verified}} * {{platforms|pc,xboxone,ps4}} The scorchbeast queen cannot summon the following scorched creature variants: [[Mothman|scorched mothman]], [[Grafton Monster|scorched Grafton Monster]], [[Mutant hound (Fallout 76)|scorched mutant hound]], [[Super mutant behemoth (Fallout 76)|scorched behemoth]], [[Frog|scorched frog]], [[Scorched|scorched suicider]] and most of the [[Scorched]] outfit variants.{{verify|verified}} ==Changelog== * With the release of [[Fallout 76 patch 1.4.0.20|patch 1.4.0.20]], enemies summoned by the scorchbeast queen can be of a higher level. * After the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' update, the scorchbeast queen received an erroneous change that made it immune to limb damage. This prevented the party from crippling its wings to force a landing. This was rectified in [[Fallout 76 patch 1.4.0.20|patch 1.4.0.20]].{{verify|patched}} ==Gallery== FO76 Scorchbeast queen.png FO76 creature scorchbeast queen.png Mounted scorchbeast queen.png|[[Mounted scorchbeast queen]] FO76 Scorchbeast Queen Concepts.jpg|Queen concept art by Katya Gudkina FO76 Scorchbeast Queen Concept 2.jpg|Queen concept art by Katya Gudkina ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Non-game}} {{Navbox creatures FO76}} {{Navbox antagonists}} [[Category:Fallout 76 boss enemies]] [[Category:Fallout 76 creatures]]

[[Spin the Wheel]] |quests = |affiliation =Snallygasters |actor = |dialogue = |edid = |formid = }} {{Quotation|The horrifying result of experiments with the experimental Forced Evolutionary Virus, the snallygaster has six limbs, numerous eyes along its back, and an extended tongue covered in acidic goo that can rapidly take down any survivors.|[[Fallout 76 loading screens|''Fallout 76'' loading screen]]}} '''Snallygasters''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] found in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background==
Experiments with recombinant strains of FEV at the [[West Tek research center (Fallout 76)|West Tek research center]] in Appalachia produced numerous failed mutations, with two exceptions. The first of these was FEVS-006443 from October 14, 2077, a Phase 2 combination strain that combined traits that resembled a number of different species. The results were considered disturbing by the scientists but provided valuable insights as to the capability of recombinant FEV. Changes included a number of ocular organs along the enlarged upper torso, a second set of arms ending in clawed digits and a large sickle-shaped claw on each inner toe. The living, stable and functioning subject was sustaining itself normally (a major accomplishment for the program) and was planned for release in [[Huntersville]] after the subsequent experiment matured.[[West Tek research center terminal entries#Report: Test Subject AM52|West Tek research center terminal entries; advanced mutations lab terminal, Report: Test Subject AM52]] The mutant was not returned to the area until January 3, 2078, when it escaped containment and the facility. The mutant procreated, leading to the emergence of snallygaster mutants across Appalachia.[[West Tek research center terminal entries#SPECIAL REPORT: CONTAINMENT BREACH|West Tek research center terminal entries; advanced mutations lab terminal, SPECIAL REPORT: CONTAINMENT BREACH]]
==Characteristics== ===Biology=== The snallygaster is a quadrupedal creature. It has two arms with three claws each, of which one is an opposable thumb, and two small limbs on the back of its body, which it usually uses to support itself while sitting. It has no proper face but has a mouth with a long tentacle-like tongue covered in acid and has multiple eyes along its back. A snallygaster will use its tongue like a whip up close and spit balls of acid at a range. The snallygaster has at least 40 eyes, two rows of teeth and thorns on its back. It has been described as being "a dragon-like demon that haunts an area outside of neighboring DC." They are easily recognizable from a distance, due to their signature clicking sounds[[Wandering storyteller]]: ''"Maybe half a year ago at a campsite not far from here, I was cookin' up a delicious, brothy stew when I heard a disgusting clicking sound nearby. Now that vile sound, it grew and grew as the thing drew nearer."''
([[Wandering storyteller/Dialogue|Wandering storyteller's dialogue]]) and the thick, pungent odor they emit.[[Wandering storyteller]]: ''"Well, then I saw a shadowy, twisted figure just beyond the forest edge. There was an unmistakeable odor as a thick, pungent stench filled my nostrils."''
([[Wandering storyteller/Dialogue|Wandering storyteller's dialogue]]) ===Gameplay attributes=== Snallygasters are almost exclusively found around highly toxic or irradiated areas in groups of up to four. When provoked, they will spit a ball of toxic slime from the mouth, dealing [[Poison|poison damage]]. They will then run to the player character and use a melee attack, either scratching or hitting the player character with their tongue. When idle and having not spotted the player character yet, they can be heard making various grunting and snorting noises. Snallygasters are immune to [[Radiation|radiation damage]] and take 150% damage when struck in the head. ==Variants== ===Snallygaster=== {{Stats creature FO76|start}} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Nascent snallygaster |form id ={{ID|0000D194}} |level =14 |perception =5 |family =snallygaster |rr =Immune |pr =0 |aggression =2 |confidence =4 |assistance =0 |items =* {{Icon|dead}} [[Snallygaster hide]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Raw asbestos]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Waste acid]] }} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Snallygaster |form id ={{ID|003BA683}} |level =22 |perception =5 |family =snallygaster |rr =Immune |pr =0 |aggression =2 |confidence =4 |assistance =0 |items =* {{Icon|dead}} [[Snallygaster hide]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Raw asbestos]] * {{Icon|dead}} [[Waste acid]] }} {{Stats creature FO76|row |name =Prime snallygaster {{seasonal}}

However, the legend of the snallygaster is more within the area of Frederick County, Maryland, and it does not match its mythological counterpart as closely in appearance. * The name snallygaster is derived from "''schnelle geister''," which is German for "quick spirits." * The snallygaster concept art was an approach to create a very mutated creature, rather than a mythical horrifying beast.[[Ray Lederer]]: ''"Fallout 76 concept art I produced for the Snallygaster. It does not match the folklore version of this cryptid but I approached it in the same way the chupacabra is really just a boiled dog or whatever instead of a mythical horrifying beast.
