'''The Interloper''' and '''the Firstborn of the Wood''' are titles which may refer to a [[Fallout 76 creatures|large creature]] worshipped in [[Appalachia]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /><ref>[[His birth]]</ref> The being writhes listlessly within the deepest chamber of the [[Lucky Hole Mine]], an abandoned mining operation on a cliff overlooking [[Watoga]], where it is cared for by the [[Cult of the Mothman|Followers of the Winged One]].

==Background==
===Lucky Hole Mine===
At some point before the war, a strange old woman visited the closed mine, and was turned away by the security team when she asked for a tour. Shortly thereafter, the mine's parent corporation sent the order to cease operations permanently. Immediately following this, the woman returned with a larger group, asking again for a tour. After this, people were spotted lurking around the premises at night, and locks were found smashed. Before long, the understaffed security team fled Lucky Hole Mine, explicitly surrendering it to this unknown group.<ref name=":0">[[Lucky Hole Mine terminal entries]]</ref> 

Following the mysterious woman's first visitation, a guard telephoned [[Fort Defiance|Allegheny Asylum]] to inquire about missing patients.<ref name=":0" /> This detail places these events no later than March 2061, when the Asylum was shut down.<ref>''[[Herald editorial on Allegheny Asylum]]''</ref>

===Omen===
On October 22, 2077, the very eve of the [[Great War]], the [[Cult of the Mothman]] set out from faraway [[Point Pleasant]] to take shelter in the Lucky Hole Mine.

The cult had conducted a ritual to summon the [[Mothman]], a harbinger of calamity.<ref>[[Sermon: Summoning the Mothman]]</ref> [[Charles (Cult of the Mothman)|Brother Charles]] experienced a vision of flood, and proclaimed that the Mothman issued a warning to the cult: seek high ground or perish.<ref name=":1">[[Sermon: Impending doom]]</ref> The preacher declared that the cult must stand on their rooftops and wait for the flood to pass, and that to disobey these instructions was an offense to the Mothman.<ref name=":1" /> 

Then, for uncertain reasons, the group abruptly travelled across the state to the Lucky Hole Mine, and began to live there as the surface world was torn asunder by nuclear war.<ref name=":2">[[Exodus (note)|Exodus]]</ref> Decades later, [[the Enlightened]] would present the narrative that it was Charles who guided the group to the safety of the mine in a tome titled ''[[Exodus (note)|Exodus]]'',<ref name=":2" /> but no contemporary evidence of this has been found.

===Jeff is summoned to the mine===
An apparent mothman cultist, [[Jeff Lane]], remained in Point Pleasant after the war. He left one holotape at his home in Point Pleasant, and one near the entrance of the Lucky Hole Mine. In the former, Lane declares his fascination with a being he calls "the Interloper." He felt he had previously harbored the notion as a "false memory," until he was told of this being "made real, deep underground" by a mad storyteller. Lane disregards the Mothman as a mere mortal creature, more similar to the human race than the Interloper and the "unknowable horrors" hidden within the subconscious mind.<ref name=":3">[[Interloper]]</ref>

Jeff Lane arrived at the Lucky Hole Mine after the War, separate from the rest of the Cult of the Mothman. He made camp at the entrance of the mine, and assessed that although he sees abundant evidence that others have also heard the Interloper's call, the entity has summoned him alone in the end. He believed the Interloper had called to him the previous night, "[[Auditory hallucinations|in visions more real than the senses]]." Lane further stated that the Interloper had chosen him as the "conduit of the unknowable," and declared "together the hidden reality becomes manifest at long last."<ref name=":4">[[The Chosen]]</ref> 

After recording this tape, he disappears from history.
===Darker worship===
As the cultists waited for the fallout to clear, some members "turned to darker worship," in a great schism which split the cult in twain. One group left the mine, ostensibly to serve the [[Wise Mothman]].<ref name=":2" /> They began to call themselves [[the Enlightened]], and founded a church called [[the Lantern]] somewhere outside the state.

However, most remained at the mine, and continued to revere the same red-eyed "holy" mothman icon they had before the war.<ref name=":2" /> They were guided by a woman known as the [[First Priestess of the Wood]] in communion with entities such as the "Great Moth" and the "Firstborn of the Wood."<ref>[[His Priestess]]</ref> This sect have been known to refer to themselves as servants of the Wood<ref>[[Cultist's final pleas]]</ref> and the Followers of the Winged One.<ref>[[Steven Scarberry/Dialogue|Steven Scarberry's dialogue]]</ref>[[File:FO76 Interloper worshippers.png|frameless|298x298px|left]]According to the series of notes spread throughout the mine, supernatural events occurred as the cultists inhabited the location, including the formation of a spring from which the cultists could drink.<ref name="Springs">[[His springs]]</ref> The notes mention that blood "wept" from His branches, and that He taught the cult to share.<ref name=":5" /> The being supposedly also told His worshippers that the faithless would deny them entry into the mine three times, before He would open the way.<ref>[[His home]]</ref>

===Current history===
By 2102, the dwellers of Lucky Hole Mine had all fled the state or died. The creature lay untended in the bowels of the mine, which was infested with various vermin. 

In 2103, the cult returned to the mine, where they continue their inscrutable rituals to this day. They kneel before the Interloper and praise him with arms raised high. The being itself rests in an obscure chamber, littered with [[mason jar|jars]], which possibly serve as a means to render blood unto its branches.<ref name=":5">[[His blood]]</ref>

Across Appalachia, these "Followers of the Winged One" built new shrines and fortified old ones. The feral red-eyed "holy" mothmen do visit them, and large clutches of mothman eggs can be seen at many of these sites. Cultist locations are instantly recognizable by the totems they build, fashioned primarily from roots and bones, identical to those found in the lair of the Interloper.  

==Characteristics==
[[File:76 gutpuker hands.png|right|frameless|267x267px]]

=== Physicality ===
The Interloper is a large dormant plant-like creature, with skin resembling stripped bark. Most of its biomass is in its tangle of "branches,"<ref name="Springs" /> and the furled pair of misshapen legs at the opposite end of its being. Its midsection appears to be an oversized humanoid torso, and it has several hand-like appendages protruding from its head and back. The place where the branches connect to the midsection resembles a mouth.

The creature will bleed if struck by the player character. Its tendrils, although rigid, occasionally move as a group, like a bush blown by wind. They seem to clench weakly and brush against the dirt.

=== Lair ===
It stirs, catatonic, on the floor of a foggy lair only accessible through a series of hidden passages. This obscure chamber is littered with jars, skeletons, and corpses. A [[sickle]] rests on the ground by the Interloper. Several effigies and totems have been fashioned from roots here. In the ceiling of this cramped space, five [[Art deco sculptures|art deco face sculptures]] loom in a semicircle, as if observing the Interloper.[[File:FO76 Interloper obelisk.png|frameless|292x292px|left]]The chamber seems to be full of [[Auditory hallucinations|strange sounds]], which change depending on where one is standing in the room. Distinct elements include insectoid buzzing, insectoid chirping, rumbling, a droning hum, a ringing chime, and a distant clattering of bells.

One of the totems in this room is a skeleton with the head of a stag mounted on a small obelisk, with moss hanging from it.

==Notes==
* The Interloper is a static object, and does not have any interaction with the player character.
* This creature is never specifically referred to as "the Interloper" in ''Fallout 76''. The name was ascribed to the creature by fans as a logical conclusion of the holotapes [[Interloper]] and [[The Chosen]]. However, it appears this naming convention was continued in the name of the [[Visitor]], and the name "Interloper" would later be used for this creature when it appeared in [[Modiphius Entertainment|Modiphius Entertainment's]] ''[[Fallout: Wasteland Warfare]]''.
** [[Jeff Lane]] only seemed to refer to the Interloper as an "entity," ascribing it no physicality whatsoever. In fact, he expressed a fascination with pursuing "great entities" and "the unknowable horrors in the peripheral vision of our subconscious minds." He considered the Mothman a mundane creature, and was disinterested in pursuing it for this reason.<ref name=":4" />
** Jeff claimed that the Interloper is capable of "calling" people through "visions"<ref name=":4" /> and mentioned that "the end of the world has awoken... something."<ref name=":3" />
** He also called the being a "watcher."<ref name=":3" /> The creature has no apparent eyes or face, but five identical [[Art deco sculptures|sculptures]] are arranged in chorus above the creature, as if silently watching it.
* Very few characters have invoked the Interloper by name.
** Aside from Jeff Lane, the supposed "story teller [...] mad by any reckoning" was the only other character to speak of "the Interloper" until the ''[[Night of the Moth]]'' update.
** [[The Enlightened]], a faction introduced in the ''[[Night of the Moth]]'' update, briefly acknowledge the Interloper in a book titled ''[[False Gods of Appalachia]]''. Wise Nathaniel the Shadowed writes the following: ''"We who would learn at the chitinous knee of the Wise Mothman, who hear his Truth and Observe the coming and going of him, must speak not of the Interloper. There is no fouler deceit than one garbed in truth. Shun its call, for it can bring only darkness."''  
*** They also describe the Interloper in ''[[Catechism of Hilary|Catechism of Wise Hilary the Scourge]]'' as an unknowable thing which turned mortals away from Truth with its "song" or "Call."
** The Vault Dwellers may ask [[Steven Scarberry|Brother Scarberry]], who was born into the Followers of the Winged One cult, about the Interloper. In a hushed tone, he responds: ''"I- I know not of who you speak. That said... It is in your best interest to drop this line of inquiry. Please. I beg of you. The response will not answer your questions. It only adds more."''
* The Interloper's lair is littered with empty jars. Jeff Lane's studio apartment in Point Pleasant is littered with jars of sugar.
* The [[Art deco sculptures|face sculptures]] in the Interloper's lair are identical to the buried faces revealed at [[Tanagra Town]] and [[Dunwich Borers]]. The same faces appear on pre-War architecture at places such as the lobby of [[RobCo Research Center]].
* Many crystal veins can be found throughout the narrow caves surrounding the Interloper and nearby to the Nave within Lucky Hole Mine. From a geological standpoint, this shows the Interloper's location within the mine to potentially be one of the oldest parts of the entire Appalachian range, as the most ancient of all Appalachian geology are [https://www.britannica.com/place/Appalachian-Mountains/Geology crystalline rocks], at roughly 500 Million to 1 Billion years old. Additionally, many lead veins can be found, which suggests at one point in the very distant past there was quite a high amount of either uranium or thorium present in the area.
* With the [[Gone Fission (update)|Gone Fission]] update, the chamber in which the Interloper resides had two baskets of fish placed within it, next to the creature's "head". 

==Appearances==
The Interloper appears {{In|FO76}}. It is also available as a printable figurine for {{In|FWW|noin}}, where it acts as a terrain piece, and has no rules for game use.

==Behind the scenes==

* The game files define the creature as an actor mesh and designate it "gutpuker."<ref>meshes\actors\gutpuker\gutpuker01.nif</ref>
* The Interloper shares some characteristics with the Veggieman, an obscure cryptid reportedly spotted in West Virginia in 1968. The creature was described as seven feet tall, made of plant matter, and telepathic. The creature purportedly hypnotized a man with its colorful eyes while it drained his blood with thorns on its fingers. This was the only reported sighting of the Veggieman.
* "Interloper" as a word is commonly understood to mean someone or something that is present in a place in which it is unwanted or not supposed to be present.

{{Infobox incomplete|FO76GD|Class, keywords, IDs}} {{Distinguish|Ultracite Titan}} {{Infobox creature |games =FO76,FO76GD |type =Creature |class = |keywords = |image =FO76GD Gleaming Depths cobra boss preview 01.png |variants = |location =[[Gleaming Depths (location)|Gleaming Depths]] |quests =[[Raid: Gleaming Depths]] |affiliation = |effects = |edid = |formid = }} The '''Ultracite Terror''' is a [[Fallout 76 creatures|creature]] in [[Appalachia]] {{In|FO76GD}}. It is the final boss of [[Raid: Gleaming Depths]], in the [[Gleaming Depths (location)|location of the same name]]. ==Background== The Ultracite Terror was originally Butch, the pet venomous snake of [[Robert Gaines|Doctor Robert Gaines]], the head of the [[Enclave (Fallout 76)|Enclave]]'s [[Project Vulcan (Enclave)|Project Vulcan]].[[Butch (note)]] It was subjected to experiments related to Ultragenesis and more generally with [[Ultracite]] in the Enclave's facility in the Gleaming Depths. During an experiment testing Ultragenesis by bombarding an Ultracite crystal with soundwaves, the snake became enraged and escaped its containment, brutally killing Dr. Gaines in the process.{{Citation needed}} When the snake initially escaped containment, it was supposedly still of a manageable size. It presumably mutated into its current massive size due to further prolonged exposure to Ultracite and radiation, as happened with other creatures such as the [[Ultracite Titan]] and the [[Scorchbeast]]s (the latter also created by Enclave experimentation). ==Characteristics== A creature hundreds of meters long, the Ultracite Terror is the largest single organism ever featured in the [[Fallout series|''Fallout'' series]]. Since being left to its own devices as the facility was first locked down and then abandoned, it has grown massively and taken on an appearance more resembling a cobra snake with its hood flaps. It has mutated two additional eyes, a multitude of new fangs, and spiky growths covering every section of its impossibly long body. The Ultracite Terror has two poison attacks, a spray attack that deals 22 ballistic and 22 poison damage and a heat seeking projectile attack that deals 233 ballistic and 233 poison damage. RD01_Enc06_Scorchtongue_AcidBreathProjectile [PROJ:00787A8A]: 22 ballistic / 22 poison
RD01_Enc06_Scorchtongue_AcidSpitProjectile [PROJ:007878E3] 233 ballistic / 233 poison ==Locations== The Ultracite Terror only spawns as the final boss of [[Raid: Gleaming Depths]]. ==Appearances== The Ultracite Terror appears only {{In|FO76GD}}. It is also mentioned in ''[[Fallout Shelter]]'' by way of the [[Ultracite Terror sword (Fallout Shelter)|Ultracite Terror sword]]. ==Behind the scenes== * During development, the Ultracite Terror was originally referred to as the Scorchtongue. This can be seen in the [[editor ID]] for its [[Fallout 76 voice types|voice type]]. * The Terror originally having been named Butch when it was still a pet snake may be a reference to [[Butch DeLoria]] and the [[Tunnel Snakes]] from ''[[Fallout 3]]''. * According to [[Matt Thomas]], the hand puppet of the Ultracite Terror shown during the 2024 [[Fallout Day Broadcast]] was not created for the broadcast, but instead the actual video the developers used to prototype the Ultracite Terror fight during pre-production.[Fallout General v21: large metal of above-average size - Knockout!]:
''"Fun fact. This is not a silly bit they shot for the video. This is the actual video we used to prototype the Ultracite Terror fight during pre-production. We've gotten great use out of this puppet."'' ==Gallery== UltraciteTerror.jpeg|Emerging UltraciteTerror2.jpeg TerrorYell.jpeg FO76GD Gleaming Depths promo-2.png FO76GD Gleaming Depths promo-3.png FO76 2025 art Nicky Barkla.jpg|Depicted on the top right in promotional art by [[Nicky Barkla]] ==References== {{References}} {{stub|FO76GD}} {{Navbox creatures FO76}} [[Category:Fallout 76 boss enemies]] [[Category:Fallout 76 creatures]] [[Category:Gleaming Depths characters]] [[Category:Fallout Shelter mentioned-only creatures]] [[ru:Ультрацитовое чудовище]]

The '''Visitor''' is a deceased [[Fallout 76 creatures|creature]] found in [[Appalachia]] {{In|FO76WL}}.

==Characteristics==
The Visitor is a pale red wood-like abomination curled on its side in a hidden chamber of [[the Deep]], accessible only by diving or [[Jet pack (Fallout 76)|flying]]. Bloody wounds appear on its surface when struck. Strange flickering black dots seem to rise from it like smoke and rapidly fade.  

By all appearances, it is simply the corpse of an unidentifiable, malformed creature which died alone in a fecund, bio-illuminated tomb. Its origin and context is unknown. No character mentions it or directly alludes to its existence.

Its head strongly resembles the hand-like blooms which emerge from splitting [[Strangler plant|strangler vines]]. It also resembles [[the Interloper]], a larger creature found within [[Lucky Hole Mine]], in that it appears to be a vaguely humanoid wooden figure in the fetal position lying on its side in an underground chamber. Both also have rigid "tendrils" in place of the head, and have small growths along two ridges down the back, resembling grasping vestigial arms. Unlike the Interloper, it does not move whatsoever, and no there is no evidence of ceremonies or gatherings in its chamber, or anywhere in the vicinity of the Deep.

==Location==
* In the bowels of [[the Deep]], hidden and insulated by flooded tunnels. 
** Bioluminescence slowly pulsates throughout the chamber, emitted by a variety of strange plants. Rare plants can be seen here, such as [[Fever blossom (Fallout 76)|fever blossom]] and [[kaleidopore]], though most cannot be harvested.
** This chamber has a small hole in the floor, which leads to a subterranean cliffside overlooking the [[Motherlode Acquisition Facility]] and its apparent moat of molten [[ultracite]]. 

==Notes==
* [[Mothman]]s emit a similar if not identical rising black particle effect from their entire bodies.
** A flayed corpse hidden nearby also emits these smoky particles. This flayed body model is elsewise only found at sites of confirmed [[Cultist (Fallout 76)|cultist]] activity.
* The Visitor is technically a static object, and does not have any interaction with the player.<ref>meshes\actors\visitor\visitorcorpse01.nif</ref> 
* There is an oil lantern adjacent to the corpse of the Visitor.
* Elsewhere in the cave, a holotape can be found, titled "[[President's eyes ONLY]]," on the corpse of a [[The Whitespring Resort|Whitespring Resort]] staff member wearing a diving suit. On the tape, the late [[James Addison]] mentions earthquakes, and gets very excited about the things he saw in the cave. However, his description of the cave is manic and inaccurate, and his plan to directly contact the president appears to be deranged. He lies face-down in a tunnel at the edge of the water, his cause of death unclear.
** James Addison's body is available as a scenery figurine in ''[[Fallout: Wasteland Warfare]]'', in the set ''"Print at Home - The Deep,"'' alongside figurines of the Visitor, the Interloper, and a [[kaleidopore]] plant. The '''vulture'''<ref>meshes\actors\vulture\vulturebodyposed01.nif</ref> is a deceased [[Fallout 76 creatures#Animals|creature]] {{In|FO76}}. It was originally [[Fallout 76 cut content|cut]], but a corpse of the vulture was introduced in the ''[[Wastelanders]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]].

==Background==
The body of a large, mutated vulture can be found pinned to a large cliff face at [[Seneca Rocks]].

==Characteristics==
The vulture is a significantly larger variant of the pre-War scavenging bird. It rivals the [[scorchbeast]] in size and is among the rarest sights in Appalachia. After doubling many times in scale compared to the pre-War equivalent, the vulture also has five, hooked talons, large upper arms and comparatively smaller hind legs. Its head is featherless, consisting of a jagged, vestigial beak. What few feathers remain are found on its back and are black in color. The [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] cannot interact with it.

==Notes==
* The vulture's NPC record has data marking it as a flying enemy, similar to the [[scorchbeast]].<ref>[https://nukacrypt.com/database/json/000041F8 NPC record]; currently a clone of the [[Vertibird (Fallout 4)|Vertibird]], which indicates it is intended as a flying creature.</ref> 
* A fully functional animation skeleton exists in the game's files.<ref>[https://nukacrypt.com/database/json/00001CA0 Body part data]</ref>
* One developer note within a vulture race keyword reads, ''"temp until we have a real vulture race"''.<ref>[https://nukacrypt.com/database/json/0010CA0B Vulture race placeholder keyword]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
* The vulture was originally a concept design for the scorchbeast, but was cut in favor of the bat model during development.<ref>[[:File:FO76 scorchbeast concept art 03.jpg|Concept art by Katya Gudkina]]</ref>
* References to the vulture still exist in the quest [[Heart of the Enemy]]. The [[viable scorchbeast DNA]] has an [[editor ID]] of <kbd>BoSz04_VultureDNA</kbd>.
* The finished model for the vulture has been present in the game's files since launch, but was only posed and placed in-game as of the ''Wastelanders'' update. Lead level designer [[Steve Massey]] jokingly described the addition as someone going "rogue" during ''Wastelanders''{{'}} development.<ref>BGS_Steve ([[Steve Massey]]) [https://web.archive.org/web/20230509180403/https://i.imgur.com/VCIKwOt.png on Bethesda Game Studios' official Discord]</ref>
* In the real world, there are two vulture species found in West Virginia - the [[Wikipedia:Black vulture|black vulture]] and the [[Wikipedia:Turkey vulture|turkey vulture]].

([[Steven Scarberry/Dialogue|Steven Scarberry's dialogue]]) is a unique [[mothman]] [[Fallout 76 characters|character]] in [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== {{Main|Mothman#Background|t1=Mothman}} As their name implies, Mothmen are mutated moths the size of men. While most are feral and red-eyed, it's believed one amaranth[[False Gods of Appalachia]]: ''"Shun this accursed creature, dear student, should you cross paths with its haunting form. Let not its amaranthine glow fool you - it shares no kinship to the Wise Mothman, and where his Truth sets loose your mind from the fetters of falsehood, this hovering nightmare binds it. There is no Wisdom to be found in such a being."''-eyed "Wise Mothman" is benevolent, and harbors some sort of profound intellect. This creature is revered by a cult called "[[The Enlightened]]." The Enlightened believe the Wise Mothman existed before the [[Great War]], and saved them from death by granting [[Charles (Cult of the Mothman)|Wise Charles the Forewarned]] the insight to take shelter in the [[Lucky Hole Mine]].[[Exodus (note)|Exodus]] In the years following complete societal collapse, there were frequent reports among the [[Charleston Emergency Government]] of people claiming to have seen Mothman.[[Speaker Poole interview]] ===The Summoning=== On October 22, 2077, the [[Cult of the Mothman]] conducted a ritual to summon the Mothman.[[Sermon: Summoning the Mothman]] One member, known at the time as [[Charles (Cult of the Mothman)|Brother Charles]], experienced a brief vision in the periphery of his senses. Supposedly, the Mothman warned him that the cult must seek high ground or perish in a flood.[[Sermon: Impending doom]] After this was announced to the cult, they suddenly crossed the state and took shelter in the mountainside [[Lucky Hole Mine]], saving them from the fallout. Decades later, in a tome titled ''[[Exodus (note)|Exodus]]'', [[the Enlightened]] would describe this event as a misguided ritual to the red-eyed "Pretender Mothman," but attribute Charles' revelation to the Wise Mothman. They also claim it was Charles who "guided his brethren to safety in the [[Lucky Hole Mine]]," a narrative complicated by the details and instructions initially proclaimed in [[Sermon: Impending doom]]. Further, they attest that the Wise One warned Charles of "fire and flood," while the preacher at Point Pleasant spoke only of a flood. === Post-War === A sect known as [[the Enlightened]] would emerge from the mine to seek the Wise Mothman as the true oracle, and condemn the other mothmen as deceivers. Brother Charles spoke of a hidden place beyond the hills they had known, and prevented the group from falling into despair. Somewhere outside the state, they founded a church called [[the Lantern]], and the prophet took on the title of [[Charles (Cult of the Mothman)|Wise Charles the Forewarned]]. The Enlightened grew into a large and stable cult. The Enlightened do not believe the Wise Mothman is a god[[Sayings of Alicia]]: ''"They cowered and prayed and made of him a God, but this was not his Truth. But some listened, and understood, and they had no fear and became Wise."'' or supernatural being,[[On the Thesis of Wallace]]: ''"Our benighted brethren among the [[Cult of the Mothman|Dim Ones]], even in their misguided worship of the Pretender, seek to know their false god better by increasing their understanding of him as a natural phenomenon. They make of him a supernal being, yet they have clamored and scrabbled for the writings of those who, like us, study the physical reality of the [[Mothman]]."''[[Catechism of Hilary]]: ''"The ignorant heard of his passing and believed not the witnesses, naming him a figment of delusional minds. Yet the Wise Mothman was no emissary from other realms, nor was he a hallucination of the senses."''
[...]

XXVII|psychic viewing session]], [[Dave (Night of the Moth)|Observer Dave]] of the Enlightened described an astral encounter with the Wise Mothman. In recording this, [[Walsh|Interpreter Walsh]] dismisses the vision as a result of Dave using chems. * The glow of the Wise Mothman is described as purple, lilac, and amaranthine.[[False Gods of Appalachia]] In-game, its eyes are distinctly magenta under controlled circumstances, but their harsh bioluminescence and rolling shadows generally make them appear lilac or purple. * The Wise Mothman NPC encountered at [[the Mothman Equinox]] uses the basic Mothman wing texture, rather than the unique Wise Mothman wing texture, which is seen on the Wise Mothman NPC encountered at [[Landview Lighthouse]].{{verify|verified}}Equinox model uses mothmanwing.bgsm instead of mothmanwingwise.bgsm This is true across all platforms, and was not changed in reruns of the seasonal event. It resembles the [[Vats of Goo]] motif and particularly the synth accompaniment of [[Fallout 4 score#Atom's Whisper|Atom's Whisper]]. * {{Atom}} A backpack flair called the Purple Mothman Eye can be unlocked through the [[Fallout 76 seasons|Atomic Shop]]. It appears to be the gory hanging eyeball of a purple mothman, which would seem to imply either the death of the Wise Mothman or the existence of multiple purple mothmen. Atomic Shop content is not specified to be canon or non-canon.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Wk3N4sO3RY&feature=youtu.be ''Fallout 76'': Is the Atomic Shop or Creation Club considered canon?]: [[Emil Pagliarulo]]: ''"Atomic Shop is a lot...we found that Atomic Shop tends to not be canon so much, it's a lot looser. Just because it's, y'know, stuff that you purchase or use Atoms get into your game that is, like... there's a big fun factor there. There's a lot of stuff in Atomic Shop that we could take out because it's not strictly Fallout canon, and then players would be bummed. Because it's in a live multiplayer game, you... it's always a judgement call, it's tough. There's a lot of stuff that's... the canon rules are a lot lighter with the Atomic Shop stuff. Paradoxically, in a business filled with paradoxes, one useful criterion in dealing with UFO cases is the fact that if the object or entity is surrounded by a glow or is seen going through the spectrum changes, it is probable that the thing seen was real or at least a real intrusion into our reality. The [[radiation]] in the environment has not affected their appearance, as they maintain consistent coats of fur. Despite the lack of external mutations, wolves still possess pointed teeth and sharp claws that are utilized to attack enemies. ===Gameplay attributes=== Wolves usually travel in packs and charge hastily at enemies to attack. Comparatively, they are overall less [[dog]]-like in their posture and movement and sport thicker patches of fur and more body fat. Since their upper body, chest and arms are not as massive, the Appalachian yao guai have a more traditional bear-like posture and gait. These yao guai are generally larger than their unmutated predecessors and are more aggressive. ===Gameplay attributes=== When yao guai are encountered, there are typically two or three in the area. Yao guai can outrun a player character unless the player character is sprinting. They have a powerful melee attack, and their strikes frequently stun the player character for a few seconds. They will pursue a player character into an open sided shed but not into a shed or building with a doorway, even if the doorway is open. When the player character enters the building, they will retreat to the edge of the area; when they detect the player character exiting the building, they will again pursue. They are sensitive to explosives and flamers. During the quest [[Flavors of Mayhem]], the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dwellers]] use the [[Karma syringe barrel (Fallout 76)|Karma syringe]] on a yao guai. ==Variants== {{Stats creature [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|The Pitt]] |affiliation = |actor = |dialogue = }} '''Fish''' are [[Fallout 76 creatures|creatures]] found in [[Appalachia]], [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]], and [[Atlantic City]] in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. [[Fallout 76 fishing|Fishing]] was added as a gameplay mechanic on June 3, 2025 with the ''[[Gone Fission (update)|Gone Fission]]'' update. ==Background== Fish survived the nuclear devastation of the [[Great War]] and are found throughout Appalachia. They are often found deceased, washed up on shores and on fish racks, collected for food. [[Jaggy|Scout Leader Jaggy]] mentions several species of pre-War fish, including bass, carp, [[catfish|bullhead catfish]], musky, perch, and walleye.[[Jaggy|Scout Leader Jaggy]]: ''"This lake was once home to numerous species of fish including walleye, musky, perch, bullhead catfish, carp... well, you get the point."''
([[P01C Tadpole LeaderJaggy.txt|Jaggy's dialogue]])[[Jaggy|Scout Leader Jaggy]]: ''"I have such fond memories of the days before the war, when the Pioneer Scouts gathered in the summer for bass fishing trips here at the lake.."''
([[P01C Tadpole LeaderJaggy.txt|Jaggy's dialogue]]) Some living fish can still be found in the waters of post-War Appalachia. Fish can be seen swimming beneath the river's surface, along the waterway between [[Beckley]] and [[Camden Park]]. While there are likely many more locations where living fish can be found in Appalachia, the murkiness of the water makes it difficult to see them without swimming into the water itself. Living fish also appear in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|The Pitt]], and can be found swimming in a shallow pool in the catacombs of the [[Sanctum]]. Both varieties of fish (living and deceased) cannot be interacted with. ==Characteristics== Fish are relatively the same size as before the war, with the addition of fleshy growths and sores on their sides. [[Delbert Winters]] mentions cooking with a variety of fish that he had never seen before while deployed, pretending they were [[catfish]] to make it more palatable.[[Volunteer training program: Food]] ==Notes== The TV aquarium CAMP object contains three fish, one of which appears to be either a tadpole or a very small eel. ==Appearances== Fish appear {{In|FO76}}. ==Gallery== Living fish in Appalachia.png|Living fish in Appalachia FO76TP Sanctum pool fishes.png|Living fish in the [[Sanctum]] 76 ETP Sanctum fish.png FO76 Fish racks.png|Fish racks FO76 Basket of fishies.png|Basket of fish FO76 Location 19521 49.png|Fish skewered by a [[stuffed polar bear]] 76 CAMP TV fish.png|[[TV aquarium]] specimens ==References== {{references}} {{Navbox creatures}} [[Category:Fish]] [[Category:Fallout 76 creatures]]
